title: 前 Xbox COO Helen Chiang 反驳外界对其离职的种种描述

Former Xbox COO Helen Chiang sets the record on her departure

Former Xbox COO Helen Chiang pushes back on characterizations of her departure
As rumors spread about her abrupt departure, Xbox's former COO Helen Chiang fires back, denying much of what has said about why the Microsoft veteran left the company.
Imran Khan
,
Contributing Editor
November 3, 2026
schedule
2 Min Read
via Mojang
Over the last few weeks,
the unfolding mystery of Xbox's COO departing after just three months on the job
has felt like a puzzle that may never be publicly solved. Thanks to a LinkedIn post from Helen Chiang breaking the silence, we at least may know why she was not let go, and it runs counter to suggestions that Xbox's first chief operating officer was fired for a policy violation.
On a post titled "Clarity is Kindness,"
Chiang takes aim at reporting that stated she had been fired from Xbox due to a policy violation. When the outlet
Eurogamer reported such
, speculation flowed wildly and freely from different corners of the internet, with threads on gaming discussion boards on Reddit and Resetera presuming that Chiang had been dismissed for leaking confidential information or harassment.
Her post outlines the different things she was "not dismissed for," all under the umbrella of no policy violation having occurred. She denies leaking confidential information, leaving to join a competitor, engaging in discrimination, bullying, harassment, insider trading, embezzlement, or other fraudulent activity.
Related:
South of Midnight director was 'always worried' about 'Rome burning' at Xbox
Finally she says she did not leave because she was passed over for a bigger role, which is an odd accusation to levy at Chiang to begin with, who had only established the role under Xbox CEO Asha Sharma three months prior.
What Chiang does not explicitly outline is why she either left or was dismissed from the company, but she does imply in the post that she finds the reasons to be unfair.
"I believe in fairness, accountability, and holding ourselves to the standards we expect of others," Chiang writes. "Those standards only mean something when they’re applied consistently. I have serious concerns about how they were applied in my case, and I believe those concerns deserve to be taken seriously."
Chiang also expresses a fear that the reporting reduces her departure to a "Nelson-level scandal." This is a reference to an internal Microsoft training video series that focuses on a character named Nelson who bumbles their way into and out of corporate problems that all employees within the company are required to watch.
The post received
a reply from Shannon Loftis
, the former VP of Xbox Game Studios. In the comment, Loftis expresses support for Chiang—who had been steering Minecraft for a decade prior to her COO role—and characterized Xbox as a "clown show." Loftis then
posted on her own LinkedIn page
doubling down on these comments, referring to Xbox as "the oppressor" and suggesting that Xbox's leadership should be investigating whoever leaked the "lie" about Chiang to the press.
Related:
Toshihiro Nagoshi's post-Sega game studio, Nagoshi Studio, shuts down after NetEase funding cuts
"I don't know what is going on with Xbox leadership right now, but it seems to bear little resemblance to the organization I used to know," Loftis writes. "The future of Xbox is cloudy indeed."
